part2.question: An important decision that you made

segments.v: I want to talk about an important decision I made last year. I decided to study business at university, not medicine. My parents wanted me to be a doctor because I am good at chemistry and doctors have a good job. But I like business more. I want to help craft villages sell their products. It was difficult to decide because I didn't want my parents to be sad. So I found information about business courses and made a plan. Then I talked to my parents. At first, my mother was worried, but then they agreed. I think this decision is important because it is about my future. Now I study harder because I have a clear goal.

part3.question: What decisions do people usually make in their daily lives?

segments.v: People decide what to eat, what to wear and how to go to work or school.
what to eat, what to wear, how to get somewhere. But there are also everyday decisions with bigger
like how to spend money, whether to exercise or rest, and how to respond to people, for example whether to reply to a difficult message now or wait. For parents, it's
decisions about children: screen time, homework, meals.

fluency.band9: Small frequent decisions → bigger everyday ones → parents' decisions → combined effect.

grammar.band9: “whether to… or…”, and concession (Individually they seem trivial, but together they shape…).

analysis.keyDifference: Band 9 moves from small to more important everyday decisions and ends with an insight about their combined effect.
